pages.lesson:
LESSON: FACTORS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers 1.1 Whole Numbers (20 lessons) • Place value and total value • reading a
Topic 1.2: Factors

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Factors. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Where do we use factors in day-to- day activities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply the Greatest Common Divisor (GC

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Factors.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Factors using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Determine divisibility of numbers using regrouping and divisibility rule worksheets
2. Write factors of composite numbers by factorisation, factor tree, factor rainbow in charts, colour charts or cards using locally available materials
3. Use factors to determine the LCM and the GCD using number cards or charts
4. Creativity and Imagination: as the learner works to create songs and poems on divisibility tests.
5. Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner applies the GCD and the LCM in solving real-life problems. Values:

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where do we use factors in day-to- day activities?
2. How do we use factors in day-to day activities?
3. How do we apply the GCD and the LCM in day-to-day activities?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Factors is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
